what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the publish-an-engine-release folder: on a builder computer, build the engine at a commit and publish it as a signed release in a feed every computer adopts from; set a Linux machine up as that builder, receiving each push to the branch; and read the builder back. The repository token reaches the one process on descriptor 3, the push secret on descriptor 4.

payload.label: Publish an engine release
payload.job: Build the engine at a commit and publish it as a signed release every computer can adopt
payload.description: On the builder: fetches the repository's branch with the token, checks the commit is on the branch's first-parent line and numbers it (its first-parent count), builds trillion-local for the builder's own rust target with the commit and number in TRILLION_RELEASE_COMMIT and TRILLION_RELEASE_SEQUENCE, packs it (with the repository's product/ folder when the commit has one) as a tar.gz named by its BLAKE3 identity, signs the entry with the builder's Ed25519 key, and adds it to feed.json newest last, keeping 32. A commit older than the feed's newest release for the same target is refused, so an older commit never wins; the same commit again changes nothing.

request_file.description: The publish config install wrote on the builder (repository, branch, base_url, work_folder, feed_folder, key_file, toolchain).

get_it: install-an-engine-builder puts this folder on the builder at /opt/engine-releases/tool
invoke.say: This runs on the builder as its builder user, from the tool folder install made; the push receiver runs it on every push, so it is run by hand only to publish again. Hand the repository token on descriptor 3, read from the vault, never in argv or a file. This publishes the branch's tip; add --commit COMMIT after the request file to publish an earlier commit the feed does not yet hold one newer than. Tell the person the sequence, target and url; a refusal for an older commit is expected and nothing changed.

payload.label: Install an engine builder
payload.job: Set up a machine that publishes a signed engine release on every merge, so a fix reaches every account without an app install
payload.description: Over SSH as root on a Linux machine the person runs: a builder user, git, Node.js and rust, Caddy serving the feed folder at https://<name>/engine-releases/ and passing push deliveries to a receiver service, and a firewall. Copies this tool there, writes the publish config, makes the signing key once on the builder (0400; it never leaves) and answers its public key, stores the repository token and the push secret as systemd credentials encrypted with the builder's host key, and starts the receiver: a push to the branch whose HMAC holds runs publish. Answers the public key, the feed's address and where to point the repository's push webhook.

request_file.description: A request JSON: builder { address, host_name }, ssh { known_hosts, identity_file? }, repository { url, branch }, keep_releases?. Its paths are read relative to it.

get_it: clone the Workshop repository (package.json repository.url) and run npm install
invoke.say: This runs on the person's computer from the root of the Workshop checkout. The builder's public name must already point at it. Hand the repository token (read access to the engine repository) on descriptor 3 and the push secret on descriptor 4, both read from the person's vault, never in argv or a file. Tell the person the public key (it goes in each place's release_feed.public_keys) and ask them to add the webhook it names to the repository themselves, content type application/json, the push event, with the same secret.

payload.label: Read an engine builder
payload.job: See whether the engine builder is receiving pushes and which release it published last
payload.description: Over SSH: whether the push receiver is running, the signing key's public half, how many releases the feed holds and the newest per target, how the last publish went, and the HTTP status of the feed at its public address.

invoke.say: No credential is needed; this reaches the builder over SSH only. A last_run with an error says what to fix; an error saying a commit is older than the feed's newest is expected and harmless.
